root_cause.text: In `net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_h323_asn1.c`’s `decode_int()` CONS path, the code checked only the 2-bit length field before calling `get_uint(bs, len)`, so a malformed H.323/RAS ASN.1 integer could make `get_uint()` read 1–4 bytes past the end of the buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, len, 0)) return H323_ERROR_BOUND;` immediately after `len = get_bits(bs, 2) + 1;`, and the CVE description explicitly states the existing boundary check covered only `get_bits()`’s 2 bits, not the subsequent bytes read by `get_uint()`.

In the CONS path it still does `len = get_bits(bs, 2) + 1;` followed immediately by `BYTE_ALIGN(bs);` and, if decoding into `base`, `unsigned int v = get_uint(bs, len) + f->lb;`. There is no bounds check on `len` before calling `get_uint(bs, len)`, which matches the root cause: only the 2-bit length field is checked, so a malformed ASN.1 integer can cause `get_uint()` to read 1–4 bytes past the end of the buffer.
